title: Battery Module Performance
shortDescription: HV battery module reports degraded performance.
fullDescription:
P0B00 indicates a single battery module within the HV pack is failing to maintain capacity or voltage in line with neighbors. The battery ECU watches inter-module spread and flags any outlier.

Replace the bad module, balance pack, and clear codes.
safetyImpact: Reduced range/MPG; can lead to pack imbalance fault.

fixSteps.title: Identify weak module
fixSteps.instruction: Per-block voltage scan with hybrid tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: HV-safe procedure; torque busbars to spec.

faq.a: Use capacity-matched modules; avoid mixing wildly different ages.

title: Battery Module Voltage Sense Circuit
shortDescription: Module voltage sense wire open or shorted.
fullDescription:
P0B01 sets when one of the per-module voltage taps cannot be read by the battery ECU. Without all taps, balancing and SOC estimation fail.

Usually a corroded sense terminal or broken pigtail inside the pack.

fixSteps.title: Open pack
fixSteps.instruction: HV-safe procedure; locate failed sense via ECU pinout.

faq.a: Will trigger pack imbalance fault eventually.

title: Battery Module Temperature Sensor Circuit Range
shortDescription: Module temperature sensor reading out of plausible range.
fullDescription:
P0B23 sets when one of the in-pack thermistors gives a reading inconsistent with neighbors (e.g., -40C while others read 25C). Usually indicates an open thermistor or broken wire.

Replace sensor inside the pack.

faq.a: Usually just sensor.

title: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
shortDescription: Secondary HV battery voltage sense circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0B3A indicates the secondary or redundant voltage sense channel on the HV battery has lost signal. Often present on packs with multiple ECU sense boards.

Diagnosis flow same as P0A8E.

faq.a: Short term yes; correct soon.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range
shortDescription: Battery pack inlet air temperature sensor implausible.
fullDescription:
P0B41 sets when the inlet (cabin) air temperature sensor for the battery cooling system reports a value out of range. The battery ECU uses this to set fan speed.

Sensor sits in the air intake duct, usually accessible behind rear seat trim.

fixSteps.title: Locate sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Behind rear seat in intake duct.

faq.a: Yes, no HV exposure for this sensor.

title: Hybrid Battery Voltage System Isolation Sense Circuit
shortDescription: Battery isolation sense circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0B7D sets when the isolation monitoring circuit (which checks HV bus to chassis insulation) cannot complete its self-test. This is a safety-critical circuit.

Do not bypass; HV system must remain electrically isolated from chassis.
safetyImpact: Loss of HV isolation monitoring; potential shock hazard.

fixSteps.title: Megger HV bus
fixSteps.instruction: Verify actual isolation; replace monitor if circuit faulty but isolation good.

faq.a: No; possible shock hazard.

title: Hybrid Battery Coolant Pump A Control Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short in HV battery coolant pump control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0B97 indicates the battery ECU cannot control the dedicated coolant pump for liquid-cooled HV batteries (Tesla, Bolt, modern PHEVs).

Unlike older NiMH air-cooled packs, Li-ion packs require active liquid cooling. Pump failure leads to derate quickly.
safetyImpact: Battery thermal management lost; charging disabled.

faq.a: Vehicle will refuse to charge.

title: Hybrid Battery Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Performance
shortDescription: Battery coolant pump not flowing as commanded.
fullDescription:
P0B98 sets when the pump runs but flow or pressure feedback is below threshold. Air in loop, partial blockage, or weakening pump are common.

Perform full bleed before condemning pump.

fixSteps.title: Bleed coolant loop
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM bleed routine via scan tool.

faq.a: Often sufficient if loop got air.

title: Hybrid Battery Positive Contactor Circuit
shortDescription: HV positive contactor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0BA0 indicates the high-voltage positive contactor (the relay that connects the HV battery to the rest of the system) has a circuit fault. Could be the contactor coil open/shorted, weld detection fault, or driver circuit problem.

Contactor faults are safety-critical — a welded contactor leaves HV bus energized after key off.
safetyImpact: HV may remain energized after shutdown; serious shock risk.

fixSteps.title: HV-safe inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Remove service plug, wait per OEM, verify zero volts.

faq.a: Absolutely not.

title: Hybrid Battery Positive Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
shortDescription: HV positive contactor welded/stuck closed.
fullDescription:
P0BA1 is the explicit DTC for a positive contactor that has welded shut. This is the worst-case contactor failure — HV bus cannot be de-energized normally.

Vehicle must be towed by a hybrid-trained shop. Contactor replacement under strict HV-safe procedure.
safetyImpact: HV bus cannot be safely disconnected; severe shock hazard.

faq.a: Excessive current under fault, e.g., short circuit.

title: Hybrid Battery Negative Contactor Circuit
shortDescription: HV negative contactor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0BBA indicates the HV negative-side contactor has a circuit fault. Both positive and negative contactors must operate together to fully isolate the pack.

Diagnosis and repair flow identical to P0BA0.

faq.a: Yes, just opposite polarity.

title: Hybrid Battery Pre-charge Contactor Circuit
shortDescription: HV pre-charge contactor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0BC0 indicates the pre-charge contactor (which charges the inverter capacitors through a resistor before main contactor closes) has a circuit fault. Without pre-charge, closing the main contactor causes a damaging inrush current.

The vehicle will refuse to enter Ready state.
safetyImpact: Vehicle won't start; potential damage to main contactor if bypassed.

faq.a: Limits inrush current to inverter caps; saves main contactor life.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Current Sensor Circuit Range
shortDescription: Pack current sensor reading implausible.
fullDescription:
P0BCB sets when the HV battery current sensor (Hall-effect or shunt-based) reports a value the ECU rejects: stuck at zero, drifted offset, or differing from inferred current.

Without accurate current data, SOC drifts and safety limits cannot be enforced.

faq.a: Try first; if drifts again, replace.

title: Hybrid Battery Module 1 Over Temperature
shortDescription: Module 1 temperature above safe limit.
fullDescription:
P0BD0 sets when battery module 1 exceeds maximum allowed temperature. The ECU will derate power and may disable HV operation.

Check cooling system first (fan/pump, intake clean), then for module-internal short.

faq.a: Allow to cool; tow if hot warnings persist.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Deterioration
shortDescription: Overall battery pack capacity below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0BFD is a generic 'pack deterioration' code similar to P0A80 used by some manufacturers. Indicates measured capacity is below acceptable level for vehicle operation.

Resolution is pack/module replacement.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Battery health scan, then module/pack replacement.

faq.a: Effectively yes; some OEMs use P0BFD.

title: Drive Motor B Inverter Performance
shortDescription: Secondary drive motor (MG1) inverter underperforming.
fullDescription:
P0C00 sets when the inverter section driving the secondary motor/generator (MG1, used to start the engine and act as generator) cannot deliver commanded performance.

Usually integrated with main inverter; full assembly replacement common.
safetyImpact: ICE start may fail; charging compromised.

faq.a: Possibly until SOC depletes, then stranded.

title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: MG1 resolver circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0C10 indicates the resolver position sensor for MG1 has a circuit fault. Without rotor position, MG1 cannot start the ICE or generate electricity.

Diagnosis flow identical to P0A40.

faq.a: No.

title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current
shortDescription: MG1 phase U current out of range.
fullDescription:
P0C2A is the MG1 (generator motor) equivalent of P0A60 — phase U current implausible. Diagnosis flow identical: megger motor windings, replace inverter or motor as indicated.

More common after coolant leak into inverter.

faq.a: MG1 starts engine and generates; MG2 drives wheels.

title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current
shortDescription: MG1 phase V current out of range.
fullDescription: P0C2B is the MG1 phase V analog to P0A61. Same diagnosis: distinguish current sensor vs winding fault via megger test.

faq.a: Less than P0C2A.

title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current
shortDescription: MG1 phase W current out of range.
fullDescription:
P0C2C is the third-phase analog. If all three set together (P0C2A/B/C), the high-side current sensor or shunt is the prime suspect.

Replace inverter assembly under HV-safe procedure.

faq.a: Common sensor block fault.

title: Generator Speed Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: MG1 speed signal lost.
fullDescription:
P0C50 sets when the speed feedback from MG1 is missing or implausible. Speed is calculated from resolver; this DTC may set alongside P0C10.

Resolve resolver/wiring fault first.

faq.a: Rarely.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Charger Communication
shortDescription: Loss of communication with on-board charger.
fullDescription:
P0C73 sets when the hybrid control or battery ECU loses CAN communication with the on-board charger module. Vehicle cannot perform AC charging until restored.

Check CAN wiring and charger LV power first.
safetyImpact: Cannot AC charge; vehicle still drivable on hybrid mode.

fixSteps.title: Check CAN
fixSteps.instruction: Verify CAN-H/L resistance and signal at charger.

faq.a: Yes; just no charging until fixed.

title: Charger AC Input Voltage Performance
shortDescription: AC input voltage out of acceptable range during charging.
fullDescription:
P0C75 sets when the on-board charger detects AC line voltage outside the spec window (typically 85-265 VAC). Could be a faulty EVSE, dirty utility power, or input sense circuit fault inside the charger.

Try a different EVSE/outlet first.
safetyImpact: Charging halted; not a safety issue if charger correctly stopped.

faq.a: First step; rules out external problem.

title: Charging System Voltage Low
shortDescription: Charger DC output voltage to HV battery below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0C78 sets when the on-board charger's DC output voltage falls below what's needed to charge the HV battery. May indicate a failing charger module, blown HV fuse inside the charger, or extreme line sag.

Typically requires charger replacement.

faq.a: Sometimes; fuse usually internal to module.

title: Charging Connector Lock Circuit
shortDescription: Charging port lock actuator circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0CA1 sets when the charge port lock solenoid (which keeps the EVSE plug locked during charging for safety) circuit is open or shorted. Vehicle may refuse to start charging or refuse to release plug.

Usually a failed lock solenoid or wiring at charge port.
safetyImpact: Plug may not lock during charging (theft risk) or refuse to release.

fixSteps.title: Manual release
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM emergency release cable to free stuck plug.

faq.a: Use emergency release pull cord (in trunk usually).

title: Hybrid Battery Pre-charge Resistor Circuit Range
shortDescription: Pre-charge resistor value out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0CB7 sets when the resistance measured during pre-charge sequence indicates the resistor has drifted or opened. The hybrid control aborts pre-charge to protect the inverter caps and main contactor.

Replace pre-charge resistor (often part of contactor pack).
safetyImpact: Cannot enable HV; vehicle won't start.

faq.a: No.

title: Battery Energy Control Module Isolation Sense High
shortDescription: HV bus to chassis isolation resistance below limit.
fullDescription:
P0CC6 sets when the isolation monitor measures HV-to-chassis insulation resistance below the safety threshold (typically 100 ohm/V or 500 ohm/V depending on standard). This is a CRITICAL safety code: an HV leak path exists.

Do not drive. Tow to qualified shop. Common causes: water intrusion (charger, motor, AC compressor), pinched HV cable, failed component insulation.
safetyImpact: Active HV leakage to chassis; severe shock hazard.

fixSteps.title: Tow only
fixSteps.instruction: Do not drive or open service plug without PPE.

fixSteps.title: Megger each HV component
fixSteps.instruction: Isolate failing leg by disconnecting one component at a time.

faq.a: Absolutely not. Tow.

title: Auxiliary Coolant Pump A Stuck Off
shortDescription: Auxiliary EV coolant pump not running when commanded.
fullDescription:
P0CCD sets when the auxiliary cooling pump (used for battery, motor, or inverter loop on EVs and PHEVs) fails to run despite command. Pump may be seized, fuse blown, or driver circuit failed.

Diagnosis: 12V test pump, check fuse, verify CAN command from ECU.

faq.a: Similar; varies by vehicle architecture.

title: Drive Motor B Inverter Voltage Sensor Performance
shortDescription: MG1 inverter bus voltage sensor reading drifted.
fullDescription:
P0CDC sets when the bus voltage sensor on the MG1 side of the inverter reports values inconsistent with the MG2 side. Indicates sensor drift or board fault.

Replace inverter assembly typically.

faq.a: Not field-serviceable.

title: Charging System Charge Port Door Circuit
shortDescription: Charge port door actuator or sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0CFB sets when the charge port door (motorized on some EVs) reports a circuit fault. Door may not open on driver request, or door-open sensor is stuck.

Fix is typically port door actuator replacement or wiring repair.
safetyImpact: Charging access compromised; not a HV safety issue.

fixSteps.title: Manual release
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM emergency release in trunk.

faq.a: Yes; fix when convenient.
